That figure still feeds gate.price_vs_anchor / kahneman.anchoring reasoning and, downstream, genius's price_usd rationale ('Buyer's stated band is $14.39-$21.59... buyer.price_psychology names a $12 ceiling'). — fix: Scout should tag each competitor entry with its marketplace and state explicitly that no Amazon-native price anchor exists this run. Buyer should treat the $4.29-$10.17/$10.17 figures as a directional, non-Amazon proxy with wider stated uncertainty rather than 'the row I see', until Amazon data is retrievable.

[genius] genius.premortem[3] (packaging tier-line jump) still assigns 30% probability to the upgraded die-cut box + shaped inner tray pushing the packed product over the 8oz small-standard tier line -- genius's own top-named packaging risk. But economics.fba_fee_usd (low 2.90 / base 3.45 / high 4.15) only widens the same-tier estimate by roughly +20%; there is still no next-tier fee scenario at the high end, so the Monte-Carlo input doesn't carry the risk genius itself flags as the most consequential packaging failure mode. Unchanged from the prior critic pass. — fix: Either fold an explicit tier-jump scenario into the high end of fba_fee_usd (price the next FBA size tier's fee), or state clearly in the assumption that the current range assumes the pin-gauge/scale-check mitigation succeeds and that a tier-jump remains an unmodeled tail risk.

[innovaty] The 'second, narrower snap-in 3mm mesh insert for tight corners' plus a replacement-SKU card is still introduced outside the formal ideas[] array -- no idea_id, no kano_class, no prior_art_risk, no thumbnail_visibility, only an ad hoc 'dimes' cost tier -- and it still does not appear in version_plan.v1_now or v2_later. Neither version's BOM in genius.json prices this extra mesh insert or card. Unchanged from the prior pass. — fix: Give it an idea_id, run it through the same TRIZ/ERRC/prior-art/thumbnail-test discipline as I1-I6, and place it explicitly in v1_now or v2_later so genius can cost it in the BOM (or drop it as aspirational scope, not actual v1 content).

[innovaty] I1 and I3 (both list N4 in improves_needs, N4 = 'real proof it was tested on small-animal bedding', severity 4) still target a need below the innovation playbook's severity>=5 funding threshold, while target_spec.needs_targeted correctly lists only N1-N3. I1 is a 'dimes' cost-tier idea; its primary justification is N1 (severity 8), but N4 riding along uncosted-and-unflagged in the same field is an internal inconsistency between what target_spec claims is funded and what the ideas claim to serve. Unchanged from the prior pass. — fix: Remove N4 from I1's and I3's improves_needs, or add a note in target_spec that N4 is addressed incidentally at zero marginal cost as a side effect, not as a funded target.

[innovaty] I3 is still self-rated 'medium' thumbnail_visibility, which per the innovation playbook's own thumbnail test means it 'needs a callout or image three' -- not reliably legible at true ~300px grid-thumbnail size. Yet listing_implications.main_image_brief and image_prompts[0] (the main/hero image) both still describe the embossed '3MM BEDDING MESH' rim text as 'readable' directly in that image ('the tray rim shows embossed raised lettering reading "3MM BEDDING MESH" catching a soft raking highlight'). Embossed, non-contrasting molded text on a tray rim is unlikely to actually read at thumbnail size, contradicting the idea's own visibility rating. Unchanged from the prior pass -- the main_image prompt was rewritten for the white-background fix but this specific claim was carried over untouched. — fix: Don't rely on I3's embossed text being legible in the grid thumbnail; let I2's color-contrast mesh carry the thumbnail-level proof, and move the 'readable molded text' claim to a full-size listing detail image (2-6), consistent with I3's own 'medium' rating.

[genius] For the v1_plus_hero window-strip BOM line, genius still states it ran its 'own one-off web search this run (not a scout fact_id, not authorized by any brief clause, just a component-price check)' citing weilinplastic.com, rapiddirect.com and protolabs.com. Unchanged from the prior pass. — fix: Strip the named-domain citations and either fall back to the knowledge-base rule-of-thumb only (as done for every other BOM line this run), or route an authorized request to scout next run and cite a real fact_id instead.

[innovaty] Two specific competitive claims still have no scout fact_id backing: (1) innovaty.packaging.upgrade_vs_category -- 'The named competitors (F1, F3-F6) ship as a bagged single scoop with no window and no explanation card' -- scout never captured any packaging detail for any competitor; and (2) the rewritten color_strategy.main_image_anchor still asserts '...a grid of white-background, black-plastic rivals' -- scout's competitor descriptions never state plastic color. The main_image gradient-background problem (K2 from the prior pass) was fixed, but this adjacent unsourced-claim problem inside the very same field survived the rewrite untouched. — fix: Soften both to 'typical category convention, not independently confirmed this session,' or have scout actually capture competitor packaging/color detail before stating it as comparative fact.

[genius] price_usd (low 16.99 / base 18.99 / high 19.99) is still only about 16% wide (low -10.5%, high +5.3% around base), materially narrower than the ~+/-30% guidance applied to every other uncertain figure this run, and it still carries no downside scenario for the case where the 'visible proof' buyer requires to accept a price above her $12 no-reason ceiling doesn't land as intended in the actual photography. [genius] The revised ad_rate.base (0.32) is now shown with full, checkable month-bucket arithmetic (75/165/280/450 units at ~70/50/30/20% ACoS unit-weights to 0.3186, correctly rounded to 0.32) -- this is a genuine, honest fix, and it reconciles cleanly with monthly_units_m6 (base 70) and monthly_units_m12 (base 140). But ad_rate.low (0.18) and ad_rate.high (0.55) are asserted narratively ('reflects a faster-than-median chasm crossing', 'reflects the pre-mortem's review-velocity obituary') without the same decomposed month-by-month arithmetic given for the base case, so their internal consistency with the forecast's own low/high share and volume ramps can't actually be checked the way the base case can. 0.18 in particular is below the knowledge base's 15-30% steady-state floor, which is only plausible if nearly the whole year sits at the very bottom of that band -- asserted, not shown. — fix: Either show the same bucketed low-case and high-case arithmetic used for the base case, or state plainly that the low/high ad_rate bounds are qualitative judgement calls rather than derived the way the base case now is.

[buyer] buyer.color_read and buyer.lifestyle_target.avoid explicitly state that 'stark clinical white... backgrounds... would anchor me back to the cat-litter category I'm actively trying to escape.' The now-corrected main_image prompt and color_strategy.main_image_anchor put the hero/grid image on a mandatory pure-white background per Amazon policy -- a sensible, necessary fix, and innovaty's own color_strategy text explains the tension reasonably (sage-green body plus white contrast mesh carrying the anchor instead of a colored backdrop). But that reconciliation lives only in innovaty.json; buyer.json's own stated preference is never caveated to note that the grid-tile background is a platform constraint, not a strategic choice. A future reader of buyer.json alone would conclude the plan is contradicting the buyer's own stated psychology. — fix: Add a one-line caveat to buyer.color_read or lifestyle_target noting that Amazon's primary image is white-background by policy regardless of brand preference, and that the 'avoid stark white' guidance applies to packaging/lifestyle imagery, not the mandatory hero image.
